items_missed: No 'How are you today?' and no agenda statement — jumped straight from 'how can I help you?' into square footage. Never asked 'sound good?'
Never got the customer's name until roughly 8 minutes in, after already discussing rates, dates and the trip fee
Never asked how many boxes — the customer raised boxes herself in her very first sentence ('or you need to call number of boxes') and it was never followed up on
Never asked about packing services for a 4,000 sqft / 4-bedroom home, and never quoted packing pricing (same hourly + materials)
Never asked about garage, storage unit, attic or balcony contents on a 4,000 sqft house
Never asked about additional stops, storage stops, elevator/parking/HOA access, or walk distance at either location
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')

Never gave an actual estimate or typical time range, despite the customer asking twice ('Would you be able to give a rough estimate of what two day move price would be like') — deferred entirely to email
Disassembly/reassembly never mentioned as included (relevant — 4-bedroom home, beds, formal dining set)
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls) and no 'take a carload' tip
No booking attempt — never asked to lock in a date even after confirming Aug 30-31 and Sept 5 availability
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the email or 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no hours / how to reach us
Used the customer's name only once, at the very end of the call
top_strength: The pricing and inclusions block was genuinely excellent — he nailed the day-of-week hourly tiers, exactly what's included, the full no-hidden-fees list, the $2,000 No Worries coverage with the in-house claims angle, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee, and all four clock rules in one clean pass. He also handled a complicated two-day interstate trip fee well, checking the mileage tier and flagging that she landed under the 220-mile break at $1,056 instead of $1,440 per truck.
coaching_note: She asked for a ballpark twice and never got one — give a range on the call (even a wide one tied to the walkthrough) instead of deferring 100% to email, and then ask for the booking. This was a two-day, multi-truck, high-dollar job with confirmed availability and no close attempt at all.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and accommodating when she had to leave for a meeting ('Hey, you're fine'), but the call is mostly long unbroken monologue with almost no affirmations, no empathy markers, and her name used once — she was reduced to 'mm-hmm' for most of the second half.
